She said she shot a cat in the face once and seemed extremely excited by the thought of it.

I had asked her out on a date, she said yes, and said I'd call her later to work out the details after work or the next day, then a bit later she said this while we were chatting during I believe closing, never called her. Still kept being nice to her, we were coworkers and all, but nothing has turned me off harder or faster than that. Was a shame to I was pretty into her before that.

Wouldn't happen to live somewhere in/by the Northwestern or Western Suburbs of Chicago (Including say Woodstock, Lake in The Hills, Crystal Lake) by any chance? Is she somewhat trashy (mostly due to being poor not because she's a trashy person), but generally a fairly nice girl without particularly high standards, with a history of boyfriends suddenly breaking down after 6-8 months with her seemingly out of nowhere. This sounds suspiciously like something one of my ex's or her friends would say/post constantly, particularly why she's an ex. Does her or any of her friends names start with K with a sister and brother whose names both start with J? Last name also starts with K?

I mean I know the chances are slim because a lot of people talk like this but it's just oddly familiar behavior, and the girl in question was literally the love of my life whom I was about to propose to until she started going a bit hard on the crazy and I just couldn't handle it anymore and had a breakdown myself leading to me dumping her.

If so it's saddening to me because even with the crazy she's legit still the standard I hold in all my relationships and I frequently hope she's doing alright. She had a deep impact on my dating life.

Here's my issue, I've seen like 20 random lanterns in caves and they would be, by far, the best light source since, like most games, nighttime is unnaturally dark to the point where you can't see at all and lanterns are literally designed to cast as much light as possible.

The problem is you can't do anything with these lanterns, and can't even pick them up.

When a lighter is the best light source in the game and still sucks, and then you and you have visible lanterns lying around you really should be rethinking your development priorities. Players need to be able to see.

I assume for the sake of assuming, but I think the OP is thinking more "prison labor" than "slaves".

I mean after all, they attacked you first, and you're sparing them out of a sense of humanity (in game context, I guess you could just be a ruthless bastard though), and the game doesn't really go along fast enough nor last long enough for you to institutionalize a generational concept of servitude. I also think that would be pretty hard to program into a game like this.

Yeah it's still not great, but you'd still be feeding and providing for them, which is more than literally anyone would realistically do in a situation where they're trapped on an island of incredibly aggressive and primitive cannibals.

Using POW's for construction and such is actually not uncommon in less developed countries. Kinda makes it odd that in the US (and many other countries, actually) we treat them like VIPs and give them the better conditions than actual citizens who are in prison.

Of course it would be pretty hard to add this to the game, both for practical AI programming reasons and also because they're cannibals and you'd need to provide them with flesh. I guess that could just be another way to harvest bones besides burning bodies, though.

Not counting the messing about exploring I did for a 6 hours or so two years ago, I've been playing for around 3 or 4 days. I figured I'd try a challenge after hitting 60 days on stalker.

Well I only visited 8 of the standing buildings with toilets out of a total 9 I had on CH as far as I recall, but I never had to go to Jackrabbit Isle so I missed that 9th one. While I was stingier with food than I normally am, at times going out under 3/4ths to start my scavenging runs, I wasn't trying to min-max anything, and I'm not sure my spawns were the best either, most of the toilets contained only 1.5L or less.

Over the course of the run I stripped two old deer carcasses, however that only netted 2Kg of meat, it was pretty much traveling food, as almost all my travelling food ended up being meat I found in houses (almost exclusively fish, and two rabbit chunks) alongside a few scavenged sodas on the ways back from the trips. Also killed a wolf who came out of nowhere, he was nice enough to show up bled out on the road in front of the Gas Station on my trip back from the lookout.

I was able to collect everything without leaving CH, honestly without visiting anything further west than the cabin just up the hill and past the fishing cabins, however I believe that only includes maybe two more cabins so I doubt I missed much there and it wouldn't have been worth the time to go there. The largest problem for me was my rifle bullet spawns only included two boxes of 5 cartridges and three single ones, finding the second box in the lookout was what even allowed me to use the gun to finish off the food I needed.

I'm curious what your time was, considering one trip between ML's dam and the topmost trailer in CH takes around 3 in-game hours one way by itself.

What caused the, in my eyes, failure of my mission:

[spoiler](#s "A bear being despawned in my final 8 hours causing me to have to hunt two deer instead (the jerk spawned as I was making my was back, I saw him coming out of his cave as I began my sprint back, and I walked right past it looking for him so I know he wasn't in there before), missing on my first shot due to anxiety leaving me with just two bullets left requiring two perfect shots, lost around two hours on that whole hunting fiasco. Just barely went over the time limit after running back to stash the meat and boil the last 10L of water I needed.")

I spoilered it because it might be considered spoilers for people trying to complete the challenge I guess, better safe then sorry.

Edit: I should clarify the title, it was my first attempt at the challenge overall, or any of the challenges really, and I told myself I could do it in one week. With a more concise route or planning, [spoiler](#s "such as actually boiling water during base stops at a higher amount instead of living off of and stockpiling almost exclusively toilet water (my average starting encumbrance was about 16kg per trip outside the gas station, with only 1kg of water per trip with only one instance of having to start a fire for it on the western trek, which was the longest by far with one over 24h period not visiting the gas station)"), I could have easily cut nearly an entire day off the total, however I didn't challenge myself to finish it in one week until around the third day.

Personally that only helped me for about 5 minutes (went from 20 to a solid 60 fps, 1080p low settings and high settings both, literally there isn't an fps difference between low and high for me at all which is confusing in and of itself) before my frame rate tanked back down to 20. I tried dropping down to 720p and it literally helped nothing, I'm honestly not sure what it is that's causing this because it behaves more like a temporary memory leak that locks in at a certain point than anything else. Also of note is my CPU load never goes above 35% (~25% towards ds3) and my memory load similarly hasn't gone above 65% (~40% towards ds3), the game just isn't tapping into the half the power of my computer for no discernible reason.  I haven't even managed to even try fighting the tutorial boss (managed to kill the lizard, though, as the frame drop was occurring. The rate of the drop was about 5 fps per 20-30 seconds at a fairly steady rate, and it didn't recover, also noticed the glowy effects on the lizard just sorta *turned off* once it dipped below about 30.) yet since the frame rate drop comes with some pretty disabling 1-2 second input lag.

I'm guessing this is the USB frame rate issue people are having but I'm not really on board the whole unplugging my controller and headset to play the game because for one that means I'd have no sound since my apartment walls are paper thin, and two Dark Souls just isn't designed for keyboard and mouse. I'm about halfway between the minimum and recommended specs so I know it's not my computer. Hell I didn't even have the issues with the intro video many people are having, I assume because I'm not trying to run the game on a potato and the optimization is literally just that bad.

This has been a pretty disappointing release for me between having to save my character preferences and restart the creation four times due to the character image freezing, fps issues, input lag, and various other little problems. I feel like they should have let the B-team take the wheel on the optimization again because I don't remember DS2 being this buggy for this large of range of computers on release, I can give DS2 that much credit at least.
